liquidbounce.module.hitSelect.descriptio: Drops hits like HitSelect (attack cancelled, swing still sent). Improves movement, reduces KB and increases crits.
liquidbounce.module.hitSelect.value.chan: Chance that an attack will be considered for dropping.
liquidbounce.module.hitSelect.value.only: Drop if target still has hurtTime > MaxTargetHurtTime.
liquidbounce.module.hitSelect.value.alwa: If you were just hit always pass (counter-hit).
liquidbounce.module.aimbotAI.description: AI Aimbot with humanization, GCD fix, silent rotations and MoveFix - undetectable.
liquidbounce.module.aimbotAI.value.fov.d: Field of view to consider targets.
liquidbounce.module.aimbotAI.value.prior: How to choose between multiple targets.
liquidbounce.module.aimbotAI.value.aimPo: Where on the hitbox to aim.
liquidbounce.module.scaffoldLegit.descri: Legit upward bridge that clicks by itself. It finds the cell that has to be filled and, only when the look the server already has cannot place it, takes the look to the center of the face with the aimbot's rotation engine - mouse lattice, trained model, silent - then clicks once the server's look traces onto that face. Minimum aim, no block-by-block stare, no Fov or Range knobs; with AutoClick the whole staircase runs on the walk alone.
liquidbounce.module.hitFlick.description: Turns the yaw off the target before a hit and back on the hit, so the extra knockback (sprint hit or Knockback) goes sideways. OnlyExtraKnockback flicks only those hits.
liquidbounce.module.aimassist.descriptio: Aim assist, not an aimbot: it never clicks and never takes the view away from your hand. It pulls a share of the way towards an enemy already under the crosshair (Assist) and damps the cursor while it glides over a hitbox (Friction).
liquidbounce.module.aimassist.value.pres: Ready-made configs (Blatant/Legit/Ghost/Closet); Custom leaves the sliders alone.
liquidbounce.module.aimassist.value.mode: Assist = magnetic pull, Friction = the cursor slows over a hitbox, Both.
Radius of the assist cone around where you are already pointing.
liquidbounce.module.aimassist.value.stre: Share of the remaining angle covered per tick.
liquidbounce.module.aimassist.value.maxS: Hard cap on a single tick, in degrees. Keeps every correction a nudge.
liquidbounce.module.aimassist.value.pitc: Share of the vertical correction relative to the horizontal one.
liquidbounce.module.aimassist.value.aimP: Where on the hitbox the assist aims.
liquidbounce.module.aimassist.value.only: Assist only while the crosshair ray crosses the hitbox.
liquidbounce.module.aimassist.value.turn: Do not fight the player: the pull waits while the mouse is pushed away from the target.
liquidbounce.module.aimassist.value.fric: How much of the cursor movement is eaten while it glides over a hitbox.
liquidbounce.module.aimassist.value.dead: Inside this angle nothing is corrected.
liquidbounce.module.aimassist.value.reac: Human reaction delay after a new target.
liquidbounce.module.aimassist.value.idle: Chance of a tick in which the assist does nothing.
liquidbounce.module.aimassist.value.gcdF: Quantize every step to whole mouse counts.
liquidbounce.module.aimassist.value.sile: Only the server sees the assist; the camera stays where you point it.
liquidbounce.module.fakeLagV2.descriptio: Holds your outgoing packets back as a real stream delay: the queue is released from the front, one client tick at a time, so the server sees a player who is simply behind instead of one who freezes and jumps. Ticks leave whole and spaced, never two inside one server tick - the pattern every 'post packet' check, Vulcan's BadPackets (Post BlockDig) among them, looks for. Latency keeps the delay constant, Dynamic follows the fight, Repel parks you where the opponent is furthest.
liquidbounce.module.fakeLagV2.value.mode: Latency adds a constant amount of delay to your packets. Dynamic adjusts your connection speed to give you advantages in combat. Repel tunes the lag to keep your opponent as far away from you as possible.
liquidbounce.module.fakeLagV2.value.dela: The amount of delay (in milliseconds) to wait for, before sending any given packet to the server. If you regularly have 50ms to a server, and this is set to 100ms, then you will effectively be playing on 150ms. Rounded to whole ticks, because a partial tick of delay is what merges two of your ticks into one server tick. In Repel it is the window of held ticks the optimizer may choose inside.
liquidbounce.module.fakeLagV2.value.tran: Higher values may make your connection more unstable, which may be a disadvantage or an advantage based on your original connection to the server. Zero gives a metronomic delay.
liquidbounce.module.fakeLagV2.value.rang: Inside the lower value the threat is maximal, out to the higher one enemies are still considered. Latency ignores it.
liquidbounce.module.fakeLagV2.value.flus: Packets that make the connection catch up: the hold drops to zero, one tick per tick, and stays there for 300ms. An interaction is therefore late by at most the hold in force when it happens, and never late again right after. There is no burst anywhere in the module - a burst merges two of your ticks into one server tick, which is exactly what checks like Vulcan's BadPackets (Post BlockPlace / Post BlockDig) flag. Empty it to keep the full delay even while interacting.
liquidbounce.module.fakeLagV2.value.adap: How fast Dynamic is allowed to change the connection speed, in milliseconds. Longer is a drifting connection, shorter is a switch.
liquidbounce.module.fakeLagV2.value.supe: Turn LiquidBounce's own FakeLag off when this module is enabled: two modules cannot share one packet queue, and that one answers every packet it does not hold with a full flush.
liquidbounce.module.fakeLagV2.value.debu: Print one line per second with the delay in use, the queue, the enemies and the ping you are effectively playing on.
liquidbounce.module.triggerBotPlus.descr: TriggerBot that presses the left button before the enemy is in range, without attacking them: it owns its crosshair ray, starts swinging (or queueing real clicks) while the target is still approaching, and only attacks once they are inside your reach. Early is a slider range drawn at every encounter, CPS a slider range drawn at every press, so nothing is constant — and nothing is ever sent to an out-of-range entity.
liquidbounce.module.triggerBotPlus.value: Ready-made configs (Legit/Closet/Aggressive); Custom leaves the sliders alone.
Reference distance when MatchVanilla is off. Set it below your real reach and let Early fill the rest.
Use the weapon's real attack range (interaction range attribute plus item range component) as base instead of Range.
Slider range: how many blocks before the attack distance the module starts pressing the left button. Drawn again at every encounter, so the moment the clicking begins is never the same.
Chance that an encounter presses early at all. 0 = the button is only pressed when the enemy is already in range.
Keep every attack inside the reach the server measures. The early click does not need it (it lives on the press), so leave it on while using the module normally.
How much of the reach stays unused. Raise it to 0.10 on a bad connection or if you still see an occasional flag.
How far past your reach an ATTACK may go. Keep it at 0: with PrePress the early click does not need to leave the reach, and anything above 0 is what a Reach check flags.

What the early press is: Swing = arm swing plus swing packet, exactly what vanilla sends when a click hits nothing; Key = a real attack-key press, resolved by vanilla on its own hit result (it is skipped whenever any entity is under the crosshair, boats and minecarts included, because that press would become a real attack on that entity); Off = no early press.
The reach the server measures (vanilla is 3.0). Every attack is capped by this, not by your client attribute, so Reach or a long item cannot drag this module into a flag.

Subtract the position drift caused by latency: the server measures the attack against two older positions — yours half a round trip old and the enemy's half of their own — so when you close in on each other the distance it computes is larger than yours. Uses both pings and the decaying maximum of both closing speeds; it only ever makes the click later. The debug line prints the value it is subtracting.
How much of the estimated drift to take into account, in percent of half the round trip. 100 is the physical estimate; raise it if flags persist, lower it if the module feels slow.

Do not attack while riding a vehicle. A boat is predicted by the client and simulated by the server, so the two positions drift apart by half a block and more: that is what a type=acacia_boat reach flag is.
Extra margin kept while riding a vehicle, when PauseInVehicle is off.
0 = the enemy must be under the crosshair ray, above 0 = a cone of that many degrees around the crosshair.
Only with ServerSafe off: lead the enemy's movement so a fast target is clicked earlier, out of reach.
How many ticks ahead the distance is evaluated (ServerSafe off only).
Random hesitation at the start of an encounter, in ticks.
Minimum attack strength before a click. 1 = only with a fully charged weapon, which keeps the damage and also prevents a double attack on the same tick.
Click rate as a slider range: a new value is drawn between the two handles after every click. 20 is one click per tick; the weapon charge (MinCooldown) still caps the real rate.
Extra random delay on top of the CPS interval, in percent. It only ever makes a click later, never earlier.
Random pause between two clicks, in ticks, on top of the CPS interval.
Only act while the attack key is held by you. Leave it off so the module can press the button by itself.
Allow the pre-trigger without line of sight.
Swing mode used for the attack.
Keep sprint on the attack (extra knockback).
Do not click while the target is still in its hurt animation, that hit would be ignored.
Which held items may attack.
Do not click while using an item.
Do not press or attack while a screen is open.
Stand down while LiquidBounce's AutoClicker is enabled, so only one module clicks.
Print every early press and every pre-trigger with the real distances.
Print every press, trigger and newly acquired target with the distances in use.
liquidbounce.module.autoPearl AI.descrip: Ender pearl for TNT sumo. In Save mode it remembers the last place you stood on and throws back onto it as soon as you are falling with nothing but air below; in Enemy mode it pearls at a player. The throw arc is fitted to vanilla's physics (the pearl inherits your own fall velocity), verified with LiquidBounce's trajectory simulation before a pearl is spent, and the rotation goes through the same mouse-lattice pipeline as the Aimassist.
liquidbounce.module.autoPearl AI.value.m: Save = get back on the platform when knocked off, Enemy = pearl into a player.
liquidbounce.module.autoPearl AI.value.t: Auto = pick the safest block top around you; Manual = throw at Point and nowhere else.
liquidbounce.module.autoPearl AI.value.p: The spot to land on, as "x y z" (the top face of the block under it). Type it, or use SetPoint.
liquidbounce.module.autoPearl AI.value.s: Switch on to store the block top you are standing on as Point; it switches itself back off. To pick a spot you are not on, type its coordinates in Point, or stand there first.
How many ticks behind the client the server's copy of your position is. Raise it if pearls land on a block side instead of its top on a laggy server.
liquidbounce.module.autoPearl AI.value.m: Fall distance needed before a save is considered. Lower reacts sooner.
Ticks in the air needed before a save is considered.
liquidbounce.module.autoPearl AI.value.v: How many blocks below are scanned for ground: if there is none, you are over the void.
liquidbounce.module.autoPearl AI.value.s: How long the remembered safe spot stays valid.
Radius searched around the remembered spot for another block to land on.
liquidbounce.module.autoPearl AI.value.l: How far the arc may drift from the chosen spot between two ticks while the aim is being held.
liquidbounce.module.autoPearl AI.value.e: How far inside the top face of a block the pearl has to land. The pearl is not a point: with a margin of 0 a throw that grazes the edge is simulated as a hit on the top face, while the real pearl hits the side one tick earlier.
liquidbounce.module.autoPearl AI.value.p: Land towards the middle of the platform instead of on its border: on the outermost block you are one knockback away from the void again, and the border is where an arc most easily clips a block side instead of its top.
liquidbounce.module.autoPearl AI.value.e: Max distance of the target in Enemy mode.
How close to the enemy the pearl has to land to count as hitting them.
Always, or only while you are in the air.
liquidbounce.module.autoPearl AI.value.r: Turn towards the solution instead of throwing immediately.
liquidbounce.module.autoPearl AI.value.m: Degrees corrected per tick while turning to the throw rotation.
liquidbounce.module.autoPearl AI.value.a: How close the rotation the server sees must be to the solved one before throwing.
Max ticks spent aiming before the attempt is given up.

Wait until the rotation the server sees matches the solved one before throwing. Off by default: the throw packet carries the rotation anyway, and waiting means the pearl leaves your hand later — which while falling is the difference between landing on the platform and not.
liquidbounce.module.autoPearl AI.value.s: Only the UseItem packet carries the rotation, the camera stays where it is.
liquidbounce.module.autoPearl AI.value.m: Movement correction used while the rotation is silent.
liquidbounce.module.autoPearl AI.value.g: Quantize the throw rotation to whole mouse counts.
Carry the rounding residual and wobble the boundary, so no two throws are identical.
liquidbounce.module.autoPearl AI.value.s: Judge every candidate with LiquidBounce's collision-aware simulation before throwing, including with the player's velocity slightly wrong: a throw that only works if the server agrees on your velocity to the tick is not a save.
liquidbounce.module.autoPearl AI.value.w: Do not throw while one of your pearls is still in flight.
liquidbounce.module.autoPearl AI.value.c: Chance that an episode actually throws, rolled once per fall or per enemy.
liquidbounce.module.autoPearl AI.value.s: Ticks the silent hotbar swap is held.
liquidbounce.module.autoPearl AI.value.p: Do not throw while a screen is open.
Do not throw while using an item.
Do not throw while riding a vehicle.
liquidbounce.module.autoPearl AI.value.c: Print every throw with the distance of the landing.
liquidbounce.module.autoPearl AI.value.d: Print the plan, the solved rotation and the simulation result.
liquidbounce.module.blockHit.description: The block hit, done for you: every click opens a block on the server for a couple of ticks and closes it again, so the hit that lands inside that window is cut while yours still lands. The block is opened on the server only - the client must not be the one using the item, or it would release the block itself and throw away your clicks.
liquidbounce.module.blockHit.value.chanc: Chance that a click becomes a block hit.
liquidbounce.module.blockHit.value.requi: Only work while the right mouse button is held, by you or by an AutoClicker's use button.
Manual = just the block hit. Lag = the block hit, then hold the outgoing packets for LagTicks so the block stays up longer on the server.
liquidbounce.module.blockHit.value.delay: Ticks between the click and the block. A block can only open on a tick, so 0 and 1 both mean the next tick.
liquidbounce.module.blockHit.value.block: How long the block stays up, in ticks. Two ticks cover the window around one click.
liquidbounce.module.blockHit.value.lagTi: Lag mode only: how many ticks the packets sent after the block opened are held back.
liquidbounce.module.blockHit.value.chatL: Print the running total every ten block hits.
liquidbounce.module.blockHit.value.debug: Print what the module decides on every click and every tick.
liquidbounce.module.fakeLagV2.value.proj: Raise the delay while an arrow, spectral arrow or trident is on a flight path that crosses you. The shot was aimed at the position the shooter renders, which is the server's one: keeping the server on an older position makes the flight cross where you were, not where you are. Works in every mode, even at Delay 0.
liquidbounce.module.fakeLagV2.value.pani: The amount of delay (in milliseconds) the dodge raises to while a projectile is incoming, and for half a second after it stops being one - the window in which the server tests the arrow against you. Higher dodges more and costs more: everything you do in that window runs on this delay.
Stairs places the block for you while you hold space; Step jumps on the space key itself.
Sneak on the edge so you never walk off it. Independent of the mode.
How far from the edge you have to be, in blocks. Drawn once per step from the range.
How far past the middle of the new block you walk before the jump. Negative jumps early.
Early clicks as soon as the jump starts; Peak waits until the jump stops rising, where the block is placed higher and the look has stopped drifting.
Ticks before the click at the edge, drawn from the range. A pause, not a rhythm.
Ticks after the jump before the click in the air, drawn from the range.
How far a click may reach. The face has to be inside it, both to look at it and to place.
The swing of the click, and whether the client, the server, or both get to see it.
Print the running total every five steps, with the misses and the average jump.
Print what the module is waiting for, whenever that changes.
The bridge clicks by itself: at the edge, holding nothing, the cell is filled and the staircase completes - walk back, jump, block on top. Off, Stairs needs the space key and Step the jump key.
Degrees per tick the look may travel toward the face. The click waits for the look, so speed costs no safety.
Share of the remaining angle the look covers each tick. 100 lands on the face at once.
The curve of the turn: Linear, Bezier or Sigmoid. Bigger error, faster correction, never a teleport.
AI uses the model LiquidBounce trained on recorded human fights; Math uses the curve above.
Which recorded-fight model drives the turn when Engine is AI.
How much of the curve's answer is mixed back in when the model drives the turn.
How much of the vertical angle is covered in one tick. A bridge face is at your feet: keep it high.
Which part of the face to look at. Closest is the one the click needs.
The camera stays yours; only the server sees the look at the block.
Derive the walk from the look the server has, so a player looking at their feet still walks where they look.
Spread the tick's turn over the frames of the tick, when the camera is ours.
Snap every turn to whole mouse counts, the lattice your real mouse lives on.
Let the rounding boundary wobble by a count, so the lattice never stalls the turn.
Whole mouse counts of hand noise on every turn. A bridge is long: keep it light.
Chance, in percent, that a turn overshoots the face by a count, the way a hand does.
How much the share of angle covered varies from turn to turn.
